The constraints include:
 1. Time‐window constraints: if we meet friend i then S[i] must lie between the friend’s available start and (available end – meeting duration).
 2. Travel constraints: if a friend i is visited before friend j then we must have enough time for i’s meeting and then to travel from i’s location to j’s location.  • Each friend “i” is available in a time window [avail_start(i), avail_end(i)] and you must meet them for at least a given “min_duration(i).”

In addition, if two friend‐meetings are both in your selected schedule then they must “chain together.” That is, if friend i is scheduled before friend j then the meeting i’s finish time plus the travel time from friend i’s location to friend j’s location must be no later than friend j’s start time.
 • One extra “chain” constraint is needed: the first visited meeting must be reachable from the start location “Presidio” – so its start time must be at least 9:00AM plus the travel time from the Presidio to that meeting’s location.

 • Finally, we set an objective on the number of visited friends (e.g. maximize the sum of selected meetings), so that we “pick the best schedule” of meetings in order to meet as many friends as possible.
